views.note: one process: a mode router, a headless core and the adapters that reach the OS — every layer edge is an ESLint wall.

views.label: Runtime
views.note: stdout is data, stderr is diagnostics; the core never touches a terminal, so a piped run behaves like an interactive one.

views.label: State
views.note: config lives in the OS state dirs and the token in the OS keystore — the only two persistence boundaries a CLI has.

boundaries.label: The CLI runtime — one process, one output port
Local state — the only persistence a CLI has

cards.title: The contract, and how it is made unbreakable
items: the contract is unbreakable and non-waivable: when a lint rule fires, the fix is to re-cut the layout — never to weaken, rename or delete the rule, and never to silence it with an eslint-disable comment, which is itself a review finding

the layer walls are pinned in lints/eslint.config.mjs: no-restricted-imports and no-restricted-globals keep the core free of process, fs, child_process, ink and @/tui; no-console forces stdout through the output port; no-eval, no-new-func and no-implied-eval make remote code impossible
scripts/check-lints.sh proves every pinned rule still fires from the marked files in lints/check/src while the clean control stays quiet, and fails if tsc --noEmit disagrees

cards.title: The three skills that ship the contract
items: cli-best-practices loads on every CLI edit and carries the contract digest: the layer table, the port table, the stream and exit-code contract, the terminal guard and the config precedence

cli-review writes a prioritized report where every finding cites the rule it breaks and shows the fix; cli-port ports a shell script or a Click/Typer/cobra CLI to a structured TypeScript CLI, porting the original tests first
the skills are instructions and reference text only: no runtime, no network, no data collection

cards.title: The runtime contract
items: stdout carries the result — text, JSON or NDJSON — and never a progress bar, a spinner, a prompt or a log line; stderr carries diagnostics
the exit code is the contract: 0 success, 2 usage, 3 authentication, 4 forbidden, 5 not found, 8 rate limited, 9 network, 10 server, 130 SIGINT, 143 SIGTERM; a usage error is 2, never 1
a non-TTY run never prompts: it fails with an actionable message and a --yes or --no-input hint; EPIPE ends the run quietly with 0 when the consumer closed the pipe

cards.title: Safety and state
items: untrusted text is sanitized before it reaches the terminal: 7-bit ESC-prefixed CSI/OSC/DCS/PM/APC and C0/C1 control characters are stripped, OSC 52 is size-capped and OSC 8 links are scheme-validated
secrets never live in config: the token goes to the OS keystore through SecretStorePort; an env var is a CI path, not the default
workspace trust is explicit: a repository's hooks, plugins, MCP servers and shell-executing settings need a confirmation, and --print never silently trusts an arbitrary repo
